title: Five Kepler passages do not match a fixed 1000 ppm dip for nine aliases of the proposed KIC 8462852 period
abstract: We test periods of 928.25/n days for integer n from 2 to 10. These periods connect the two shallow dips reported for KIC 8462852. Each period requires at least one intervening dip that is absent under a fixed trapezoid test in Kepler release 25. The nine tests use five distinct passages. Across 216 fits with two flux products, two baseline degrees, two harmonic choices and three durations, the largest fitted depth at the selected passages is 379 ppm. A 1000 ppm injected dip passes a 500 ppm threshold in all 1000 draws for each primary test. Other noise block sizes give recovery rates of at least 98.1 percent. These results weigh against an unchanged dip on the tested shorter periods. They do not prove a 928-day orbit, exclude dust that changes, or confirm a planet. The passage selection is exploratory. The noise ranges are conditional diagnostics. Both flux products share exposures. No independent telescope confirms this result.

display.caption: Five distinct passages test nine shorter periods. Blue points are 0.2-day means of SAP flux after the fitted baseline and harmonics are removed. Red lines show the trial 1000 ppm dip. Repeated panels share the same data. This comparison does not establish the longer period.

citations.reason: Reports the shallow pair and motivates the fixed dip and period scale.
Recent recurrence model allows changes in dip families; our fixed-profile test does not test that model.
Earlier campaign study tests two deep dip shapes. We test different shallow events and their shorter period aliases. No code or data are reused.
